Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided extracted content, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious setup.py install-time execution, or suspicious PEP 517 build hooks.
  • The server.entry_point and mcp_config.command/args in mcpb/manifest.json appear to be MCP server runtime configuration, not install-time automatic execution.
  • The execution steps in .github/workflows/*.yml and docker/Dockerfile appear to be CI/CD and container build behavior, not malicious code that runs on package installation or Python interpreter startup.
  • model_rebuild() and imports in src/sqllens/agent/core/__init__.py look like library initialization and are not tied to credential theft, exfiltration, or loader behavior.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence of broad environment-variable harvesting, .env scraping, SSH key collection, cloud credential discovery, CI/CD token theft, or wallet-file discovery was identified. SQLLENS_LLM__API_KEY and anthropic_api_key appear to be documented application configuration.
  • **Exfiltration / staging:** No evidence of harvested-file archiving, temp staging, base64 staging, webhook/C2/raw-IP upload, or paste/drop-service exfiltration was identified. dist/*.tar.gz appears to be a normal release artifact pattern.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of cron jobs, systemd units, launch agents, shell profile edits, startup-folder registration, or self-reinstall/background persistence loops was identified.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes token abuse, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions workflow injection, or package-registry token reuse was identified. Use of GITHUB_TOKEN, OIDC, GHCR login, and image signing in GitHub Actions appears consistent with normal release/container publishing workflows.
  • **Obfuscation / loader:** No evidence of eval, exec, compile, marshal, pickle, compressed/encrypted payload loaders, or downloader stubs was found in the provided files.
  • The raw.githubusercontent.com URL appears to be a JSON schema reference for the MCPB manifest, with no supporting evidence that it is used as a malicious payload or exfiltration endpoint.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Within the provided file set, no hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, wheel/sdist mismatch, typosquatting evidence, or sudden malicious dependency insertion were identified.
  • .github/workflows, docker/Dockerfile, mcpb/manifest.json, and documentation files appear to be normal project development/distribution support files and are not supply-chain attack evidence by themselves.
  • Dockerfile pip install --user ".[all]", GitHub Actions python -m build, PyPI Trusted Publishing, and cosign download/signing appear to be ordinary build and release workflow behavior.
